purpose: A09 evidence for FP-018. Paired loopback timings with their uncertainty, recorded so the numbers can be read honestly. These are 127.0.0.1 measurements of total time to a flushed, hash-verified file; they do not model RTT, loss, blocked UDP, slow storage or competing traffic, and they support no Internet speed claim of any kind.

versions.curl: curl 8.21.0 (x86_64-w64-mingw32) libcurl/8.21.0 Schannel zlib/1.3.2 brotli/1.2.0 zstd/1.5.7 libidn2/2.3.8 libpsl/0.21.5 libssh2/1.11.1 WinLDAP

reading: Fetchpath is slower than the curl baseline on loopback: 55.9 ms mean against 35.5 ms excluding the first pair, and its spread is far wider (sd 16.3 against 2.1). The first Fetchpath run of the session took 152.5 ms against a 37.4 ms best, which is process and allocator warm-up rather than transfer cost. No acceleration claim is made or supported. What these runs do establish is correctness and instrumentation: every one of the 14 outputs matched the fixture hash, and the adaptive path stayed inside its configured budget in every run.

http3.reason: packaged libcurl reports HTTP/3 unavailable; policy records http3_unavailable and falls back without a false attempt

notCovered: Any non-loopback path. No RTT, loss, blocked-UDP or competing-traffic conditions were exercised.
Tail percentiles. Seven pairs support a mean and a spread, not a p95 or p99.
A packaged HTTP/3 endpoint. The packaged libcurl reports HTTP/3 unavailable, so the fallback is capability-driven and untested against a real h3 server.
Storage other than this machine’s. Publication cost on a slow or network volume is unmeasured.
